title: Short- and Longer-term Impact of Cancellation of High Speed Rail Project on Singapore Government’s Revenues and Expenditures
what_it_is: Short- and Longer-term Impact of Cancellation of High Speed Rail Project on Singapore Government’s Revenues and Expenditures

sections.label: HSR costs and GST
sections.summary: Singapore will meet HSR Bilateral Agreement obligations and seek compensation if Malaysia terminates the project; GST increase funds recurrent spending, not infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Unless the project is terminated, Singapore has to meet our obligations under the legally binding HSR Bilateral Agreement (BA) and will continue to incur costs in this regard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the event that Malaysia causes the project to be terminated, Singapore will exercise our rights under the BA and international law, including with respect to compensation for costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The increase in GST was never meant to finance lumpy investments in infrastructure in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The main drivers for rising Government expenditure in recent years, and going forward into the future, are healthcare, security and social spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: These are broad-based, structural increases in recurrent spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we have to raise recurrent revenues, of which the planned GST increase is one component, to pay for these ongoing needs year after year.

sections.label: Infrastructure funding and GST rationale
sections.summary: Singapore saves ahead and borrows for large infrastructure like Changi T5, HSR and RTS, so the GST increase rationale is unaffected by the HSR outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, where possible, we will save ahead and set aside funding for such investments through initiatives like the Changi Airport Development Fund and the Rail Infrastructure Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Second, we will finance infrastructure through borrowing by Statutory Boards and Government-owned companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This will apply to larger investments that can generate economic benefits over many years, like the Changi Airport Terminal 5, the HSR and the JB-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Therefore, the underlying rationale for the GST rate increase is not affected by the outcome of the HSR Project.
